title: Selective-activation verdict for latent older-adult human assets
objective: Test whether retirement-transition capture, use-case-informed discovery or social referral can reduce source-discovery cost enough to preserve LATENT HUMAN-ASSET LEGIBILITY / ACTIVATION as a broad private regenerative formation.
truth_rules: RETIREMENT CAPTURE MAY PRESERVE EXISTING LEGIBILITY RATHER THAN DISCOVER NEW VALUE
USE_CASE_INFORMED DISCOVERY MAY COLLAPSE INTO ORDINARY DEMAND MATCHING
SELF_SELECTION AFTER ROLE EMERGENCE WEAKENS THE NEED FOR A GENERAL DISCOVERY INTERMEDIARY

evidence.fact: Xuchang maintains one-person-one-file retirement records and captures professional specialties and interests while immediately moving newly retired cadres into silver-talent pools.
Changxing uses retirement ceremonies/'first retirement class' as a direct entry point for newly retired adults into youth-support/service groups.
Bazhong similarly captures one-person-one-file records and uses organization recommendation, home invitation and self-nomination to move newly retired cadres into silver-talent structures.

what_it_solves: reduces later rediscovery work for institutionally known retirees
what_it_does_not_prove: discovery of ordinary retirees outside organized employment/cadre systems
discovery of tacit/everyday assets the person cannot self-describe
mechanism_a_retirement_transition_captur.verdict: PRESERVE_AS_PUBLIC/INSTITUTIONAL LEGIBILITY MECHANISM__NOT BROAD PRIVATE EDGE

evidence.fact: Minqing collected 43 effective public-service needs and matched 39 projects using a demand-order → platform-dispatch → talent-accept → evaluation model.
A Hunan community combines silver-resource mapping with resident questionnaires/grid visits to form a service-demand list and reports a 98% demand response rate in 2025.
Xinghua uses 2,819 pooled retirees but converts demand into 12 defined projects across six governance/service domains and runs resident-order/community-dispatch/volunteer-accept routing.

what_it_solves: prevents mapping assets with no plausible use
narrows search to capabilities relevant to recurring demand classes
what_it_does_not_prove: a unique hidden-asset infrastructure beyond ordinary service/demand routing
discovery of previously unnameable everyday assets at scale
mechanism_b_use_case_informed_discovery.verdict: EFFECTIVE SELECTIVE ACTIVATION__BUT MOSTLY EXISTING COMMUNITY DEMAND ROUTING

mechanism_c_social_referral.state: REFERRAL CHANNEL REAL__REGENERATIVE SUCCESS-REFERRAL LOOP NOT EVIDENCED

evidence.fact: Current silver-talent discovery uses resident nomination, organization recommendation, unit recommendation and personal self-nomination.
Adjacent community models show that core participants can bring in residents who later become core participants, proving social propagation can exist in local governance settings.
evidence.evidence_role: adjacent mechanism evidence, not hidden-asset economic proof

missing_evidence: successful elder activation generating another high-value elder referral
portable trust beyond the original community
mechanism_c_social_referral.verdict: NOT SUFFICIENT TO SAVE BROAD FORMATION

ordinary_hidden_asset_survival.state: SOME CATEGORY-SPECIFIC SURVIVAL__NO GENERAL LOW-COST DISCOVERY ENGINE

evidence.fact: Fengtai's Silver Workshop deliberately discovers scattered older adults with crafts and retired-engineer knowledge across 38 community pilots, showing non-credentialed/less formal assets can be surfaced.
The Silver Artisan youth-elder project explicitly targets previously overlooked community non-heritage crafts and uses young volunteers/social workers to activate product/class/channel value.

ordinary_hidden_asset_survival.limitation: These cases require category focus plus community/social-organization access. They do not demonstrate a generic low-cost mechanism for discovering arbitrary hidden older-adult assets.

evidence.fact: Current reporting shows ordinary/low-age retirees entering new roles such as short-drama acting, livestreaming, dance teaching/commercial performance, silver broadcasting and interest-community operations once the role/market form is visible.

self_selection_counterevidence.implication: When a new role becomes socially legible and accessible, some older adults self-select without a dedicated hidden-asset discovery intermediary. This further weakens the need for a universal supply-discovery layer.

reason: cheap transition capture mostly preserves already-legible institutional identity
use-case-informed discovery converges on existing demand-routing models
social referral is real but not success-generated/self-replenishing
ordinary hidden assets survive only in category/community-specific structures
when roles become visible, self-selection can surface supply directly
high private value density remains strongest in already-legible professional segments

primary_decision.preserved_as: SUPPORTING FRICTION / SENSOR / SUBSYSTEM WITHIN CATEGORY-SPECIFIC FLOWS
primary_decision.not_killed_factually: Retirement can hide capability and active elicitation can recover it.
primary_decision.killed_commercial_claim: There is not enough evidence that generic discovery/legibility of older-adult assets is itself a broad, privately sustainable regenerative river.

youth_retiree_family_status.explanation: Demoting generic hidden-asset discovery does not kill the user's young × retired life-world thesis. It only rejects one attempted riverbed. Other intergenerational formations may still exist where two durable potentials already create repeated partial flow.

next_action: Return to broad everyday-life formation sensing with a white active portfolio. Preserve young × retired as an important calibration family but do not force the next formation to be hidden-asset discovery. Search for large/replenishing everyday actor populations with durable complementary state disequilibria, repeated informal/expensive leakage, a recurring missing edge and a natural Demand Pump. Prefer ordinary visible life over institutional/program examples. Do not start from jobs, products, gigs or explicit buyer tasks.
